newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech 1997 budget high on December parl't agenda.
newsitem.headline: Czech 1997 budget high on December parl't agenda.

text.p: The Czech parliament is expected to discuss the government's draft 1997 balanced budget as an early item in this month's session which begins on December 10, the parliament's press office said on Monday.

In the proposed agenda put forward by the chairman of the lower house Milos Zeman, the budget's second reading is the sixth item, making it likely to be discussed in the first two days of the session.
A third and final reading cannot come sooner than 24 hours after the second reading is approved, but should come before the close of the session expected to last through December 18.
The agenda still must be approved at the beginning of the session.

On October 9, the lower house gave the minority centre-right coalition a key victory, approving the first reading of the budget, as four deputies of the opposition Social Democrats broke party ranks to vote for the draft.

The vote sparked a major rift between Zeman, who is also chairman of the Social Democrats, and the party's dissenting deputies who include budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner, and party first vice-chairman Karel Machovec.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's fifth straight balanced budget plan, proposes equal revenue and expenditure of 549.1 billion crowns next year, after a 1996 balanced budget plan which forecasts a revised total of roughly 491 billion crowns.

The approval of the first reading locked in the overall 1997 budget totals, although amendments can be made on items on both the expenditure and revenue sides in the final two readings, as long as the overall total remains the same.
